topic: Blood type personality (혈액형 성격설): before MBTI, Koreans read personality from ABO blood type; stereotypes A careful/timid, B selfish/free, O outgoing, AB genius-or-odd; origin Furukawa Takeji 1927 Japan paper, revived by Nomi Masahiko 1971 book; Korea boom 2004-05 incl. film My Boyfriend Is Type B (2005); Gallup Korea Feb 2023 (n=1,501): 57% believe (67% in 2002/2012, 58% 2017), under 1% don't know own type (5% in 2002), 36% of believers say consider it for dating/marriage, O favorite 49%, no blood-type pattern in married couples or self-rated MBTI tendencies; Nawata 2014 >10,000 Japan/US: blood type explains <0.3% of personality
title: In Korea, Your Blood Type Was Your MBTI

slides.headline: Before MBTI, Koreans asked **your blood type.**
Four types, **four personalities**
slides.body: Type A is careful and a bit timid. Type B is free and selfish. Type O is outgoing. Type AB is either a genius or a little strange.

slides.headline: Everyone **knows theirs**
slides.body: Fewer than 1 in 100 Korean adults don't know their own blood type. So the question always has an answer.

slides.headline: It came **from Japan**
slides.body: A Japanese professor first tied blood type to temperament in 1927. A 1971 bestseller in Japan brought the idea back, and it crossed to Korea.

slides.headline: The **Type B man**
slides.body: In the mid-2000s the craze peaked. A 2005 Korean rom-com, My Boyfriend Is Type B, was about a girl warned off a man because of his blood type.

slides.headline: It even reaches **dating**
slides.body: Among Koreans who believe it, about 1 in 3 say it's good to consider blood type when dating or choosing a spouse.

slides.headline: What science **says**
slides.body: A 2014 study of more than 10,000 people in Japan and the US found blood type explains less than 0.3% of personality.

slides.headline: of Korean adults **still believe it**
slides.body: That's from a 2023 Gallup Korea poll. In 2002 it was 67%. The fad faded. The belief mostly didn't.

slides.headline: Then came **MBTI**
slides.body: The same poll compared blood types with MBTI-style traits. No pattern. Now Koreans ask for four letters instead of one.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Four small glass vials of red liquid in a rack, blurred behind the text.

caption:
Before Koreans asked for your MBTI, they asked for your blood type. A is careful, B is selfish, O is outgoing, AB is a genius or a weirdo.

Science says there's nothing to it. More than half of Korean adults still believe it a little.

Do you even know your blood type?
reply: Korea's mix, from the same 2023 poll: A 34%, O 28%, B 26%, AB 11%. And O is the favorite: about half of believers picked it as the best type. Is blood type something people talk about where you live?
fact_check: 1·9장: MBTI 이전 유행 = 2002년부터 갤럽 조사가 이어진 혈액형 성격설, MBTI는 2020년대 유행(09-16편).
2장: 유형별 고정관념은 통념 소개(A 소심, B 이기적, O 활발, AB 천재 아니면 이상). 사실 주장 아님.
4장: 후루카와 다케지 1927 논문(Psychological Research), 노미 마사히코 1971 책(en 위키·BigThink). '한국으로 건너옴'은 en 위키 서술.
5장: 2004~2005 열풍·2005년 영화 B형 남자친구(이동건·한지혜, 2005-02 개봉) — 주간경향·en 위키.
6장: 갤럽 2023, 믿는 855명 중 36% '연애·배우자 선택 때 혈액형 고려하는 게 좋다'.
7장: Nawata 2014, Japanese Journal of Psychology 85(2), 일본·미국 1만여 명, 68문항 중 65개 차이 없음, 설명력 0.3% 미만(PubMed 25016835).
9장: 갤럽 2023 MBTI 4지표 자기평가 분포가 혈액형별로 비슷(오차 범위 내). 기혼 966명 부부 혈액형 조합도 상관 없음.
reply: 갤럽 2023 분포 A 34·O 28·B 26·AB 11, 믿는 사람 중 O형 선호 49%.
